completed_tasks.name: Gaussian interpolation table
completed_tasks.details: 512-entry table from SPU silicon dump. Three-way verified against psx-spx, DuckStation, Mednafen.

completed_tasks.name: Downsampler with pitch counter
completed_tasks.details: Decimates 44.1 kHz input to configurable voice rate (4,000–44,100 Hz) via pitch counter. Default 22,050 Hz (0x0800).

completed_tasks.name: Gaussian 4-tap upsampler
completed_tasks.details: Full pitch-counter-driven Gaussian interpolation with variable interpolation index. Reads decoded ADPCM samples and produces 44.1 kHz output.

completed_tasks.name: Anti-aliasing filter
completed_tasks.details: Single-pole IIR pre-filter before decimation. Cutoff tracks voice pitch. Toggleable on/off.

completed_tasks.name: GUI controls
completed_tasks.details: Voice Rate knob (4,000–44,100 Hz), Gauss toggle, Anti-Aliasing toggle in toolbar area.

completed_tasks.name: Standalone play/stop fix
completed_tasks.details: Engine processes silence when stopped instead of skipping. Prevents stale decimator/Gaussian state on resume.

decisions.decision: PS1 SPU voice path added to ADPCM chain
decisions.rationale: ADPCM was missing the downsample and Gaussian interpolation that every PS1 voice went through. Full chain: downsample → ADPCM encode/decode → Gaussian upsample.
4 kHz confirmed as lowest used rate (PS1 BIOS boot bell). 44.1 kHz = passthrough (no decimation). Default 22,050 Hz — most common PS1 music rate.
Anthony wants aliasing as a creative option. Filter off = raw decimation with foldback artifacts. Filter on = clean decimation.
Toggle allows comparing raw ADPCM vs Gaussian-smoothed output.
Explicit instruction — downsampler/Gaussian only affect the ADPCM bus.

next_action: Beta artifacts rebuilt and ready to distribute. Repo is private. Await tester feedback.
